summary: Configured node1 to disable core payloads for system-managed service accounts while retaining systemd crash logging. The policy survived reboot; node1 is healthy with no failed units.
actions_performed: Reloaded the system manager and validated a controlled SIGSEGV under the `systemd-resolve` account.
Safely rebooted node1; boot ID changed from `6001d24d-a752-4a58-a0b2-082876564497` to `44f08f85-4cc4-443f-82ca-cfd33cc521a4`.
Verified all running local service-account processes have soft and hard core limits of zero.
Confirmed journald and systemd-coredump logging remain active and no core payload was created by the post-reboot probe.

evidence.requirement: Disable core dumps for local service accounts
evidence.summary: Shows the persistent manager configuration, effective default limit, post-reboot inherited zero limit, zero generated payload files, and zero soft/hard limits for every running local service-account process.
Controlled crashes retained PID, UID, signal, and unit metadata in the journal while explicitly reporting that no coredump was generated.
Captures the healthy baseline, acknowledged native reboot schedule, changed boot identity, recovered services and retained journal data, persisted policy, running system state, and zero failed units.
